headline: Data Centers Pay Own Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, primarily data centers, bear more of the costs for new grid infrastructure and capacity, rather than shifting these expenses to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration, Senator Louise Lucas, Dominion Energy (with amendments).
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: A Virginia bill, HB 1393 (and similar SB 253), aims to shift the cost of new distribution infrastructure and capacity auction prices onto high-load energy users like data centers, potentially saving residential customers around $5.52 a month. Governor Spanberger amended the bills to allow the State Corporation Commission to determine fair cost allocation, ensuring data centers pay their share and protecting residential ratepayers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This bill requires local water authorities to report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to data centers, increasing transparency on their water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage to the Department of Environmental Quality, with numbers to be publicly available on a website by January 1, 2027. This aims to provide transparency on the industry's water consumption, which has been a growing concern for communities and environmental groups.

headline: Localities Gain Data Center Siting Control
short_summary: This bill empowers counties, cities, and towns to implement stricter zoning ordinances for data centers, including noise mitigation and siting standards, in response to community concerns.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, homeowner associations, environmental groups, Senator Danica Roem (for similar state-level measures).
news_headline: Manassas Tightens Data Center Zoning Rules Amid Noise Concerns
news_summary: Manassas City Council unanimously approved a zoning ordinance amendment to tighten development rules for data centers, addressing resident complaints about noise, visual impacts, and proximity to residential areas. This local action reflects a broader trend in Virginia, where HB 153 (and similar SB 94) introduces new siting requirements and mandates impact assessments for data centers.
